decision.summary: The Fed raised its policy rate by 25 basis points, to 0.25% to 0.5%. The vote was 8-1. Dissenting: James Bullard.

changes.quote: Job gains have been strong in recent months, and the unemployment rate has declined substantially.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Job gains have been solid in recent months, and the unemployment rate has declined substantially.”

changes.quote: Inflation remains elevated, reflecting supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic, higher energy prices, and broader price pressures.

tone_quotes.quote: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1/4 to 1/2 percent and anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate.
Inflation remains elevated, reflecting supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic, higher energy prices, and broader price pressures.
Job gains have been strong in recent months, and the unemployment rate has declined substantially.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 14.51% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.19% and moved +4 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.76% would rise by about $6.82 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 3.9%, and employers added an average of 532k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 7.9% over the past year (February 2022); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 5.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 6.8% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +10 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 2.24%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.37% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 0%, cut 0%, hike 100%.
